Petitioner has filed this petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, clai
ming the compensation amount of Rs.40,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.

2. Petitioner case is as Follows:
That on 28.06.2024 at about 9.50 AM., he was riding the motorcycle beg.
Reg.No.KA-11-EU-0039 in Bengaluru University road, Jyanabharathi Campus,
wherein the driver of the Car bearing Reg No.KA-04-MN- 2317 drove it, with high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the two wheeler and caused accident, in the accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

He was shifted to Vijay hospital for first aid, later he was shifted to Nandi Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient for the accidental injuries and he has spent Rs.3,00,000/- for his treatment.
3. Petitioner stated that he is 22 years of age and he was working as a salesman and he was earning Rs.30,000/- per month,

Further he stated that the accident occurred due the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and the jurisdictional police have registered Cr.No.220/2024 against the driver of the offending vehicle.

Petitioner alleged that the Respondent no.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and he insured his vehicle with respondent no.1 and respondent No.3 is holder of the policy and accident caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and as such they are liable to pay the compensation with interest and he prayer this tribunal to award the compensation amount with interest by allowing the petition.
4. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, Respondent No.1 appeared through its counsel filed power and written statement.
Respondent No.2 & 3 have not chosen to contest the petition and they placed exparte.

Respondent No.1 admitted the issuance of insurance policy to the vehicle of respondent No.2 and contended that insured has violated the policy conditions and prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.

5. Petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and examined the medical record keeper and orthopedic surgeon as PW.2 & 3, produced and marked 26 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 26 and they are fully cross examined.
6. Respondent no.1 evidence taken as nil as prayed for.
7. I have heard the arguments from the counsels appearing for both the sides.
I have perused the same along with entire records.

7.1 Counsel appearing for petitioner has relied on the following authorities:
1. Rudra Vs Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited & another - (2011) 11 SCC 511.

8. On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following :
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 28.06.2024 at about 9.50 AM., he was riding motorcycle beg.

Reg.No.KA-11-EU-0039 in Bengaluru University road, Jyanabharathi Campus, wherein the driver of the Car bearing Reg No.KA-04-MN-2317 drove it, with high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the two wheeler and caused accident, in the accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries as alleged in the petition ?
2.
Whether respondent no.1 proves that the insured has violated the policy conditions as contended in the written statement ?
3.Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?

if so, what is the quantum and from whom?
4.What order or award?

9 . After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
Issue no.1: In the affirmative Issue no.2: In the negative Issue no.3: In partly affirmative Issue no.4:
As per final order for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 to 3 :- I have taken these issues together for common discussion so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW.1 being the petitioner, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.

Petitioner has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, police intimation, sketch,
mahazar, Final report, discharge summary, notice and reply given U/s 133 of IMV Act which are at Ex.P.1 to 12.
11.
On careful perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents, it is evident that one Sri.Ashok Kumar S/o Prathiban was the driver of the offending vehicle as on the date of the accident.

Mahazar, sketch,
IMV report, final report establishes the involvement of the offending vehicle and the negligent act of the driver in the alleged accident.

Further ExP.10 is the reply notice given by respondent No.2 wherein he admit that Ashok Kumar was the driver of his vehicle and he was having valid driving Chandan Gowda D C vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125841006/

sentences.text: 12. In the cross-examination of PW-1, he denied the suggestion that he himself dashed against the offending vehicle and denied the suggestion that there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Nothing worth has been elicited to disprove the petition allegation.
The alleged negligent act of the petitioner is not suggested to PW-1.
Respondent No.1 has failed to establish its contention that accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner.
Admittedly as per the wound certificate and discharge summary petitioner has sustained grievous injuries that is right hand humerus fracture and right leg tibia fracture.

13. The final report which is at Ex.P11 is filed after investigation and it is the prima facie proof of the accident and the involvement of the offending vehicle and rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly the police records cannot be doubted and disbelieved as it has reached the finality.

14. Petitioner has tender the wound certificate, discharge summary as per Ex.P.7,12, the entry therein reveals that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries that is right hand humerus fracture and right leg tibia fracture, ORIF with plating to humerus was done on 30.06.2024 and ORIF with nailing for tibia is done on 28.06.2024.
Further petitioner has taken treatment for the accidental injuries as inpatient for 4 days.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following heads.

15. Pecuniary damages (Medical expenses) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization,
Medicines, Transportation, Nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure:
16.
Petitioner took treatment at Nandhi hospital.
Evidently nothing is elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disbelieve the fact that he has sustained the grievous injuries in the alleged accident and he took treatment for the same.
Inasmuch, discharge summary, wound certificate and the medical reports issued form the hospital has to be accepted.
Admittedly petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient for 4 days, and underwent two surgeries for fractures and he has tendered medical bills of Rs.2,44,619/- as per Ex.P.19.
Further for the attendant charges, transportation, nourishing food, he might have spend some more expenses.
Therefore I award Rs.20,000/-, in total petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,64,619/- under this head.
Loss of income during laid up period.

17. The petitioner has tendered salary slips as per Ex.P.15, resignation letter and its acceptance letter as per Ex.P.16 & 17, and it is not disputed nor denied by the respondent No.1 and nothing worth is elicited from the mouth of PW-1 to disprove the aforesaid documents.
As per the pay slip for the month of June 2024, he was drawing monthly salary of Rs.20,000/- per month.
The monthly salary is assessed as Rs.19,800/- after deducting the professional tax.
Considering the accidental injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, I am of view that the petitioner might have lost income for one month.

Therefore I award Rs.19,800/- as compensation Chandan Gowda D C vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125841006/

sentences.text: Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
18. The petitioner has examined the Orthopedic surgeon Sri.S.A.Somashekara as PW-3.
He deposed that petitioner has underwent two surgeries for humerus fracture and right leg tibia fracture and petitioner has 26.28% of whole body disability as per Ex.P25.

He further deposed that there is no shortening of limbs for the petitioner and inplants are still there in the body the petitioner and additional two surgeries are required to remove the inplants and the cost of surgery is around Rs.50,000/-.
I have perused the evidence of PW-3 wound certificate, discharge summary, medical reports given by the hospital, X-ray etc.
Evidently petitioner has not examined the doctor who has treated him in the hospital.

Petitioner sustained grievous injuries that is right hand humerus fracture and right leg tibia fracture, ORIF with plating to humerus was done on 30.06.2024 and ORIF with nailing for tibia is done on 28.06.2024.
Further doctor has admitted that fractures are united and petitioner is having no swelling and infection and he has no further complication.
The oral testimony of PW-3 corroborates with Ex.P.25 and 26.
Admittedly petitioner has no functional disability.
The percentage of loss of earning capacity due to accidental injuries is different from the percentage of physical disability due to accidental injuries.
Considering the medical reports and oral testimony of doctor and the authority relied on by the petitioner at Sl No.1 of para 7.1, the whole body disability of the petitioner is assessed as 24%.
The age of petitioner as on the date of accident is 22 years as per the entry in Aadhar card and DL which are at ExP.13 & 14.
The multiplier applicable to this case is "18".

Non-Pecuniary damages (General damages) (IV)Damages for pain and sufferings and loss of amenities:
19.
It is undisputed fact that petitioner has sustained grievous injury.
During the hospitalization and rehabilitation period, he might have undergone lot of pain and sufferings and due to accidental injuries and two surgeries.
Therefore I award Rs.40,000/- under these conventional heads.

V) Loss of Amenities :-
20.
The petitioner has to forego certain amenities available for him.
Therefore I award Rs.40,000/- as compensation under this head.
As per the oral testimony of PW-3, another surgery is required for the petitioner, for the removal of implants.
The estimated cost of the surgery is not tendered.
Tentatively petitioner is entitled for Rs.50,000/- for the additional two surgeries.

23. Liability:

The insurance company has not disputed the validity of the policy of the offending vehicle, on the other hand, they have failed to established its defence that insured has violated the policy conditions.

As such respondent No.1 is the liable to pay the compensation amount with interest, respondent No.1 is directed to deposit compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of this order.
Hence with the aforesaid discussion based on the evidence placed on record, I am answering Issue No.1 the affirmative, issue No.2 in the negative and issue no.3 in partly affirmative.
24. Issue No.4:

ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor vehicle Act,1988, is partly allowed with cost.
